findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh:2505-2510 (13j's background writer poll) and :2560ish (13k's twin), against .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh:1845-1892 (verify_actor_marker_took_effect, the R2-F1 fix)
findings.evidence: THE CLAIMED FIGURE DOES NOT REPRODUCE, TWICE. `bash .claude/scripts/tests/runner-completeness.test.sh` run standalone, twice, back to back: run 1 -> `Total: 433 assertion(s)` / `FAILED: 3` / rc=1 / 10:37.17 wall (13:06:59Z-13:17:36Z); run 2 -> `Total: 433 assertion(s)` / `FAILED: 3` / rc=1 / 10:21.96 wall (13:20:53Z-13:31:15Z). SAME THREE LEGS BOTH TIMES: 13j.2, 13j.7, 13k.2. Run 1 emitted one `child setpgid ... Operation not permitted` line; run 2 emitted ZERO (grep -c setpgid = 0) and failed identically, so that was incidental, not causal. ROOT CAUSE, PROVEN WITH A MATCHED CONTROL RATHER THAN INFERRED. The 13j/13k background writer polls for the intended spec's start marker with a bound of 60 iterations x 0.2s = 12.0s, then runs `bd comment` UNCONDITIONALLY whether or not the mark appeared - the expiry is never itself asserted. I measured time-to-mark on an identical 72-spec fixture WITH A SEEDED STORE (so the canary ARMS, which is what 13j/13k do and what my first probe wrongly omitted - I corrected my own probe rather than reporting its answer): shipped runner 13.39s and 13.39s; a mutant that bypasses ONLY the self-check CALL (`verify_actor_marker_took_effect "$BEADS_ACTOR"` -> `ACTOR_SELFCHECK_OK=1`; non-vacuity checked: differs from shipped, parses under bash -n) 7.95s and 8.44s. Four arms, run back to back under the same ambient load. So the R2-F1 self-check adds ~5.2s at ARM time - more than the ~2.5-2.8s its own header claims, because it is a full bd init + bd create + bd comment + dolt log cycle, not just an init - and that pushes the fixture from ~8s (comfortably inside the writer's 12s bound) to ~13.4s (outside it). The writer then fires into whatever spec happens to be running at wall-clock 12s: observed `stub-065.sh` (run 1) and `stub-069.sh` (run 2) where `zz-slow-clean.sh` was expected, and `stub-063.sh` / `stub-070.sh` for 13k - all in the 63-70 band of 72, exactly where a fixed 12s bound lands in a ~13.4s sequence. THE SHIPPED MECHANISM IS NOT AT FAULT AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD: 13j.1, 13j.4, 13j.5, 13j.6 all PASS, so the store move IS detected, the writer IS named, the target issue IS named, and the Degraded count IS exactly 1. Only `which spec` is wrong. Every NEW leg added this round passes - 19a-19e and 20a-20d are all green. THE REGRESSION IS NEW THIS ROUND: at my round-2 measurement the full tier read 401/401 rc=0 with 13j and 13k both passing, and verify_actor_marker_took_effect did not exist then.
findings.description: The round-3 fix for R2-F1 broke three legs of the SAME task (dhh7) added in round 1, and the tier is red (rc=1) on the host the full L1+L2 run is about to happen on. The failure direction is loud rather than silent, which is the better direction - but a control that cries wolf is one people stop reading, which is this runner's own stated reason for STRICT_SECTIONS existing. REQUIRED FIX, two parts: (a) make the poll's expiry an EXPLICIT, NAMED failure ('the intended spec never signalled within Ns - this leg's premise did not hold') instead of writing anyway, because right now a premise failure surfaces as a confusing assertion about the wrong spec three legs later, which is exactly how I spent the expensive part of this review; and (b) size the bound against what the fixture actually costs - an armed canary pays two `dolt sql hashof('HEAD')` queries per spec across 72 specs, plus the new ~5s ARM self-check. Measured need on this host: >13.4s against a 12.0s bound. HONEST CAVEATS, because the margin matters: the shortfall is ~1.4s, so this is host- and load-sensitive, and a concurrent full L1 tier (pid 68418, 50+ minutes elapsed) was running throughout all of my measurements. But both arms of the control were measured under that same load, back to back, and the WITH/WITHOUT split (13.39s vs ~8.2s) is far larger than the observed repeat variance (0.00s and 0.49s). I am NOT claiming the implementer's 433/433 was fabricated - a 12% margin flips between hosts and moments, and its own contract disclosed that it had not observed the real unfiltered run's floor line either.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh COMPLETENESS-FLOOR block, the two `Completeness floor: HELD` printf arms, read against the same file's `--filter` DISARMED arm and its STRICT_SECTIONS refusal block
findings.evidence: FIRST, R2-F2 IS GENUINELY FIXED AND I REPRODUCED MY OWN ROUND-2 COUNTEREXAMPLE AGAINST THE SHIPPED RUNNER. Declared {stub-001,stub-002,stub-003} via the EXPECTED-SPEC-FILES sentinel splice, on disk {stub-001,stub-002,zz-undeclared}, EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT completely unset: rc=1, `COMPLETENESS FLOOR BREACH: 3 spec file(s) discovered, 3 declared - COUNTS MATCH but the SETS DO NOT (a rename-shaped drift: one file left, a different one arrived)`, naming zz-undeclared.sh as arrived and stub-003.sh as departed. At round 2 that identical fixture read HELD. THE HATCH ITSELF IS NOT TOO WIDE, and I checked every question that was put to me. Reachability: repo-wide sweep finds EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT in exactly two files (run-tests.sh reads it, runner-completeness.test.sh sets it) plus dhh7's own completion record; no CI env block sets it (.github/workflows/test.yml declares only STRICT_SECTIONS=1, BD_SHIM_ONLY=1, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); no Makefile recipe sets it (`make test` is a bare `bash run-tests.sh`); no hook script sets it (workflow-doctor.sh matches EXPECTED_SPEC only in two comments about EXPECTED_SPECS); it is not in my live environment. Parse safety, all twelve arms measured against the shipped runner: unset -> strict; empty string -> strict; `1`/`TRUE` -> strict; `0`/`no`/`false` -> legacy; and `0 `, ` 0`, `False`, `off`, `2` all -> rc=2 with `EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT must be 1/yes/true or 0/no/false (got ...)`, i.e. malformed values fail CLOSED, never silently off. Override scoping reproduced on this host's bash 3.2.57 rather than accepted: an exported base of 0, a `VAR=1 func` prefix on a function that spawns a child bash inside a command substitution, and plain calls before and after - child sees 0, 1, 0, 1, 0 and the parent stays 0 throughout; same for the direct-invocation shape; posix mode is off and neither file sets it. Harness containment: I joined backslash-continued lines and scanned every runner invocation in runner-completeness.test.sh - 0 of them lack a fixture CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so the export can never weaken a real-project run; and specs are launched as `bash "$test_file" ... &`, never sourced, so a spec cannot mutate the parent's already-parsed EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT_ON. Pairing quality: 19e.7-19e.11 prove load-bearing, not merely read - 19e.7/8 use `env -u` for the TRUE unset default and get rc=1 plus the SETS DO NOT message, while 19e.9/10/11 use =0 on the IDENTICAL fixture and mutant and get rc=0 plus HELD plus no breach text. Verdict AND output both flip. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG IS NARROWER AND I MEASURED THE CONVENTION BEFORE ASSERTING IT. On a passing fixture the two modes are byte-identical: a full normalised diff of both runs is zero differing lines, 19 lines each. I first read that as a disclosure gap, then tested whether `announce the mode` is this file's convention at all - it is NOT: STRICT_SECTIONS=0 vs =1 is also byte-identical on a clean run. The real convention is `announce when the weaker mode lets something through`, and STRICT_SECTIONS honours it exactly - with a section actually skipped, =1 prints six extra lines ending `Do not read this run as full coverage: it is not.` EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT=0 prints nothing extra in its equivalent case: on the same-count rename it prints `Completeness floor: HELD (3/3 specs discovered and executed; 0 skipped a section; 3 assertion(s) executed)` and exits 0, with no caveat at all - while `--filter`, which likewise cannot make the full claim, prints `Completeness floor: DISARMED (--filter run; this summary describes a subset, not the tier)`. Leg 19e.10 asserts that HELD text as expected behaviour, so the harness locks it in.
findings.description: MY ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED, PLAINLY: the hatch is NOT too wide, I do not recommend reworking it, and I agree with the implementer's rejection of renaming ~30 sections' fixtures - that trade would cost a great deal to buy nothing those sections were ever testing. What is worth one line is the caveat. In the single case where the two modes differ - a same-count rename under STRICT_ON=0 - the run makes the unqualified claim `Completeness floor: HELD` over a set whose identity it did not check, which is the one shape this file's own convention (measured above, not assumed) says should carry a caveat. SUGGESTED FIX, one printf arm: under EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT_ON=0 print a distinct line - e.g. `Completeness floor: HELD BY COUNT ONLY (N/N; EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT=0, so declared-vs-discovered NAMES were not compared - a rename-shaped drift would not be caught by this run)` - and have a leg assert the two modes' floor lines DIFFER. That also makes 19e.10 assert something stronger than the deception it currently pins. Not blocking: no real invocation can reach STRICT_ON=0, malformed values fail closed, and the degraded mode is a reversion to the pre-R2-F2 behaviour rather than a new hole - pure adds and removes are still caught.

findings.evidence: Both headers state that the only setters are `runner-completeness.test.sh's run_l1/run_l1_env_bdactor helpers`. Neither helper contains an assignment. run_l1's own header says so in as many words - `EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT is NOT pinned here, unlike STRICT_SECTIONS above - it does not need to be` - and run_l1_env_bdactor's says `EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT is inherited from this file's top-level export`. MEASURED, with the counting method stated: `grep -o` gives 21 instances and `grep -c` gives 21 lines (no line carries two). Nine are real assignments: one `export EXPECTED_SPEC_FILES_STRICT=0` at :292, file top level, outside every function; seven prefix `=1` overrides at :3825, :3840, :3983, :4080, :4103, :4132, :4145; one prefix `=0` override at :4019 (19e.9, the deliberate-misbehaviour leg). A tenth match at :4020 is an assert_eq message string, not an assignment. There is also one `env -u` at :4012. The brief I was given said `6 occurrences in that file`; I could not reproduce that number by any counting method and am reporting mine with the commands.
findings.description: A documentation inaccuracy in the one place whose entire purpose is to let a future reader audit who can turn this guard off - and it points at two functions that do not do it, so a reader who greps run_l1 for the assignment finds nothing and is left unsure whether the header is stale or something else sets it. Worth noting that the implementer's OWN completion contract has it right (`exported to 0 exactly once near the top of runner-completeness.test.sh`), so the code header disagrees with the contract rather than with reality. FIX: say `set once at runner-completeness.test.sh's top level (a single `export`), inherited by every subprocess it spawns; the sections needing strict override it with a prefix assignment at their own call site`. Not blocking.

findings.location: the phantom background-task notification the dhh7 implementer reported and refused
findings.evidence: NOTHING IN THE TREE OR THE STORE CARRIES CONTENT ATTRIBUTABLE TO IT. Six independent checks: (1) docs/reviews/ holds exactly claude-workflow-plugin-gytz-r1.json and -r2.json for this task - no r3 existed before the one this artifact creates; (2) `find . -name '*gytz*'` outside .git returns only my own r1/r2 artifacts and the gate's own .qa-tracking state files; (3) gytz carries exactly two REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 records, iteration=1 and iteration=2, both reviewer=qa-claude model=claude-opus-5[1m], and no third; (4) no qa-approved label on gytz or on any of dhh7/wuu8/90av/9hv4 - gytz reads devops,qa-blocked,qa-gate-entered,rubric-pending and the four members all read qa-pending, every one of which I can account for; (5) the store's last 400 commits carry exactly two actors, `username` (250) and `edk0` (32), with no unattributable third; (6) every file modified in the last 24h is accounted for - bd's own backup rotation, the gate's .qa-tracking state, the 189 fixture mirrors from the central sync, and the files from today's landed commits. All five tasks are clean in .beads/quarantine.tsv, checked before reading any comment as evidence. AND THE ANOMALY ITSELF RESOLVES, AS ROUTING RATHER THAN ATTACK, ON DIRECT EVIDENCE. The implementer compared two UUIDs drawn from DIFFERENT namespaces. `0a003deb-24d9-4e17-ae5c-5ba6844c746b` is not a per-agent transcript id: that scratchpad directory was created Sep 5 12:43:38, nine seconds after the root `claude --resume` process (pid 61653) started at Sep 5 12:43:29, and it holds 459 entries spanning Sep 5 to now - including MY round-1 artifact (Sep 16 16:31) and round-2 artifact (Sep 16 18:27), written by two different QA spawns, plus the coordinator's own 3o4r notes. It is the ROOT SESSION's shared scratchpad. `77a1576b-bdc1-43b4-aa48-1136c0474105` is the background-task output namespace for that SAME tree: it holds 276 task outputs including my own from this very session, and one of its entries is a symlink `acd7461df86b2787d.output -> .../0a003deb-.../subagents/agent-acd7461df86b2787d.jsonl` - i.e. the 77a1576b namespace links directly into the 0a003deb tree. That jsonl's first record reads `sessionId: 0a003deb-24d9-4e17-ae5c-5ba6844c746b`, timestamp 2026-09-16T12:48:26.308Z - sixteen seconds before my own gate-enter at 12:48:42Z, and the file is still growing. It is THIS QA spawn. So: the notification was for round 3, created by the ROOT orchestrator (which is why the type is one a subagent cannot spawn - CLAUDE.md is not violated), under the same session as the implementer, and it referenced a review round that did not exist yet because that round is this one.
findings.description: Not a defect in the change set, recorded because it was asked for and because the answer should be durable. The leading explanation is background-task notification delivery scoped to the session TREE rather than to the initiating agent, so a sibling subagent receives notifications for spawns it did not make. The implementer's own transcript stopped being written at 12:46 and the QA spawn was created at 12:48, so the two were adjacent. I cannot prove the negative from inside one agent - I can only show that nothing landed, and I checked six ways. The implementer's decision to refuse and flag was exactly right: from inside its own context it had no way to compare the namespaces, and 'a notification naming a review round that does not exist' is a correct thing to stop for. Worth an orchestrator-side confirmation that notification routing is tree-scoped by design, so the next agent that sees this can dismiss it in one step instead of a full sweep.
